---
title: "Geography is a Systems Variable"
subtitle: "Same cluster, same model, same duration: does location change the cost?"
description: "Compare identical training runs across four grid regions to discover whether geography matters more than hardware choice or training duration for carbon footprint."
categories: ["ops", "intermediate"]
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import mlsysim  # installed via `pip install mlsysim` (see workflow)
from mlsysim import Systems, Infrastructure
from mlsysim.solvers import SustainabilityModel, EconomicsModel
from mlsysim.systems.types import Fleet

Engine = mlsysim.Engine

_grids = Infrastructure.Grids
_g_quebec = _grids.Quebec
_g_norway = _grids.Norway
_g_iceland = _grids.Iceland
_g_france = _grids.France
_g_eu = _grids.EU_Avg
_g_germany = _grids.Germany
_g_texas = _grids.Texas
_g_us = _grids.US_Avg
_g_china = _grids.China_Avg
_g_iowa = _grids.Iowa
_g_india = _grids.India_Avg
_g_poland = _grids.Poland

_node_count = 32
_duration_days = 30
_short_days = 10
_fleet = Fleet(
    name="256-GPU Training Cluster",
    node=Systems.Nodes.DGX_H100,
    count=_node_count,
    fabric=Systems.Fabrics.InfiniBand_NDR,
)

_sust = SustainabilityModel()
_econ = EconomicsModel()

_r_q = _sust.solve(fleet=_fleet, duration_days=_duration_days, datacenter=_g_quebec)
_r_n = _sust.solve(fleet=_fleet, duration_days=_duration_days, datacenter=_g_norway)
_r_us = _sust.solve(fleet=_fleet, duration_days=_duration_days, datacenter=_g_us)
_r_p = _sust.solve(fleet=_fleet, duration_days=_duration_days, datacenter=_g_poland)

_carbon_q = _r_q.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000.0
_carbon_n = _r_n.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000.0
_carbon_us = _r_us.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000.0
_carbon_p = _r_p.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000.0

_energy_q = _r_q.total_energy_kwh.magnitude / 1000.0
_energy_p = _r_p.total_energy_kwh.magnitude / 1000.0
_water_us = _r_us.water_usage_liters / 1000.0
_water_p = _r_p.water_usage_liters / 1000.0

_ci_ratio_pq = _g_poland.carbon_intensity_g_kwh / _g_quebec.carbon_intensity_g_kwh
_ci_ratio_pn = _g_poland.carbon_intensity_g_kwh / _g_norway.carbon_intensity_g_kwh
_ratio_pq = _carbon_p / _carbon_q
_ratio_pn = _carbon_p / _carbon_n

_r_10p = _sust.solve(fleet=_fleet, duration_days=_short_days, datacenter=_g_poland)
_carbon_10p = _r_10p.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000.0
_ratio_10p_30q = _carbon_10p / _carbon_q

_carbon_price = 50
_tco_q = _econ.solve(fleet=_fleet, duration_days=_duration_days, grid=_g_quebec)
_tco_p = _econ.solve(fleet=_fleet, duration_days=_duration_days, grid=_g_poland)
_ccost_q = _carbon_q * _carbon_price
_ccost_p = _carbon_p * _carbon_price
_tot_q = _tco_q.tco_usd + _ccost_q
_tot_p = _tco_p.tco_usd + _ccost_p
```

## The Question

A `{python} _fleet.total_accelerators`-GPU cluster (`{python} _node_count` `{python} _fleet.node.name` nodes) trains a model for `{python} _duration_days` days. Where that cluster is located makes no
difference to latency or throughput, which the hardware fixes. For carbon emissions, water
usage, and total cost of ownership, does geography matter, and if so, by how much?

::: {.callout-note}

- **Quantify** the gap between the cleanest and dirtiest electricity grids
- **Compare** geography vs. training duration as levers for sustainability

::: {.callout-tip}
## Background: Grid Carbon Intensity

Every kilowatt-hour of electricity has a carbon cost, measured in grams of $\text{CO}_2$ per kWh
($\text{gCO}_2/\text{kWh}$). This number depends entirely on how the electricity is generated. Representative profiles from `mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids` span nearly two orders of magnitude:

| Region | Primary Source | Carbon Intensity | PUE |
|:-------|:---------------|:-----------------|:----|
| `{python} _g_norway.name` | Hydroelectric | `{python} f"{_g_norway.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} gCO2/kWh"` | `{python} f"{_g_norway.pue:.2f}"` |
| `{python} _g_quebec.name` | Hydroelectric | `{python} f"{_g_quebec.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} gCO2/kWh"` | `{python} f"{_g_quebec.pue:.2f}"` |
| `{python} _g_france.name` | Nuclear | `{python} f"{_g_france.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} gCO2/kWh"` | `{python} f"{_g_france.pue:.2f}"` |
| `{python} _g_us.name` | Mixed (gas, coal, renewables) | `{python} f"{_g_us.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} gCO2/kWh"` | `{python} f"{_g_us.pue:.2f}"` |
| `{python} _g_iowa.name` | Coal and gas reference | `{python} f"{_g_iowa.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} gCO2/kWh"` | `{python} f"{_g_iowa.pue:.2f}"` |
| `{python} _g_india.name` | Coal-dominated | `{python} f"{_g_india.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} gCO2/kWh"` | `{python} f"{_g_india.pue:.2f}"` |
| `{python} _g_poland.name` | Coal-dominated | `{python} f"{_g_poland.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} gCO2/kWh"` | `{python} f"{_g_poland.pue:.2f}"` |

The range is wide (`{python} f"{_ci_ratio_pq:.0f}×"` in grid carbon intensity between Poland and Quebec, and `{python} f"{_ci_ratio_pn:.0f}×"` between Poland and Norway). This tutorial quantifies how that spread interacts with facility PUE and whether it matters more
than other levers such as training duration or hardware choice.
:::

## 1. Setup

```python
import mlsysim
from mlsysim import Engine
```

---

## 2. Two-Region Comparison

The first comparison runs the same training job in two locations: `{python} _g_quebec.name` (`{python} f"{_g_quebec.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} gCO2/kWh"`, PUE `{python} f"{_g_quebec.pue:.2f}"`)
and `{python} _g_poland.name` (`{python} f"{_g_poland.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} gCO2/kWh"`, PUE `{python} f"{_g_poland.pue:.2f}"`). The `{python} _fleet.total_accelerators`-GPU fleet, the model, and the `{python} _duration_days`-day duration are identical. The only variable
is where the electricity comes from.

```{python}
from mlsysim import Systems
from mlsysim.solvers import SustainabilityModel
from mlsysim.systems.types import Fleet, Node, NetworkFabric
from mlsysim.core.units import Q_
from mlsysim.show import table, info

# 256-GPU cluster: 32 DGX H100 nodes
fleet = Fleet(
    name="256-GPU Training Cluster",
    node=Systems.Nodes.DGX_H100,
    count=32,
    fabric=Systems.Fabrics.InfiniBand_NDR
)

solver = SustainabilityModel()

# Quebec: hydroelectric grid
res_quebec = solver.solve(
    fleet=fleet, duration_days=30,
    datacenter=mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids.Quebec
)

# Poland: coal-heavy grid
res_poland = solver.solve(
    fleet=fleet, duration_days=30,
    datacenter=mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids.Poland
)

carbon_q = res_quebec.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000  # tonnes
carbon_p = res_poland.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000
ratio = carbon_p / carbon_q if carbon_q > 0 else 0

table(
    ["Region", "Carbon (tonnes CO2)"],
    [
        ["Quebec (Hydro)", f"{carbon_q:.1f}"],
        ["Poland (Coal)", f"{carbon_p:.1f}"],
    ]
)
info(Ratio=f"{ratio:.0f}x")
```

Same cluster. Same model. Same `{python} _duration_days`-day duration. Because Poland's grid carbon intensity is `{python} f"{_ci_ratio_pq:.0f}×"` higher than Quebec's (`{python} f"{_g_poland.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f}"` vs. `{python} f"{_g_quebec.carbon_intensity_g_kwh:.0f} gCO2/kWh"`) and its facility PUE is `{python} f"{_g_poland.pue / _g_quebec.pue:.2f}×"` higher (`{python} f"{_g_poland.pue:.2f}"` vs. `{python} f"{_g_quebec.pue:.2f}"`), the total carbon footprint differs by **`{python} f"{_ratio_pq:.0f}×"`** (`{python} f"{_carbon_p:.1f}"` tonnes vs. `{python} f"{_carbon_q:.1f}"` tonnes $\text{CO}_2$). The difference comes from a location
decision, not from an algorithmic optimization.

---

## 3. All-Region Sweep

The next sweep expands the comparison to four grid regions in the Infrastructure Zoo,
adding energy consumption, water usage, and PUE to the picture.

```{python}
grids = [
    mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids.Quebec,
    mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids.Norway,
    mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids.US_Avg,
    mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids.Poland,
]

region_results = {}
rows = []
for grid in grids:
    r = solver.solve(fleet=fleet, duration_days=30, datacenter=grid)
    energy_mwh = r.total_energy_kwh.magnitude / 1000
    carbon_t = r.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000
    water_kl = r.water_usage_liters / 1000
    region_results[r.region_name] = r
    rows.append([r.region_name, f"{energy_mwh:,.1f}", f"{carbon_t:,.1f}", f"{water_kl:,.1f}", f"{r.pue:.2f}"])

table(["Region", "Energy (MWh)", "Carbon (t)", "Water (kL)", "PUE"], rows)
```

Total facility energy varies across regions from `{python} f"{_energy_q:,.1f} MWh"` in `{python} _g_quebec.name` and `{python} _g_norway.name` (PUE `{python} f"{_g_quebec.pue:.2f}"`) to `{python} f"{_energy_p:,.1f} MWh"` in `{python} _g_poland.name` (PUE `{python} f"{_g_poland.pue:.2f}"`). Water consumption ranges from `{python} f"{_r_q.water_usage_liters / 1000.0:.1f} kL"` in closed-loop cold-climate hydro facilities to `{python} f"{_water_us:,.1f} kL"` (`{python} _g_us.name`) and `{python} f"{_water_p:,.1f} kL"` (`{python} _g_poland.name`). Combined with grid carbon intensity, emissions span `{python} f"{_carbon_n:.1f} t"` in `{python} _g_norway.name` and `{python} f"{_carbon_q:.1f} t"` in `{python} _g_quebec.name` up to `{python} f"{_carbon_p:.1f} t"` in `{python} _g_poland.name` (`{python} f"{_ratio_pq:.0f}×"` vs. Quebec and `{python} f"{_ratio_pn:.0f}×"` vs. Norway).

---

## 4. Geography vs. Training Duration

The trade-off between training longer in a clean region and shorter in a dirty region
shows up in a comparison of `{python} _duration_days` days in `{python} _g_quebec.name` against `{python} _short_days` days in `{python} _g_poland.name`.

```{python}
# 30 days in Quebec
res_30d_quebec = solver.solve(
    fleet=fleet, duration_days=30,
    datacenter=mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids.Quebec
)

# 10 days in Poland (1/3 the training time)
res_10d_poland = solver.solve(
    fleet=fleet, duration_days=10,
    datacenter=mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids.Poland
)

c_q = res_30d_quebec.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000
c_p = res_10d_poland.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000

table(
    ["Scenario", "Carbon (tonnes CO2)"],
    [
        ["30 days in Quebec", f"{c_q:.1f}"],
        ["10 days in Poland", f"{c_p:.1f}"],
    ]
)
info(Ratio=f"{c_p/c_q:.1f}x")
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Key Insight

**Geography is a larger lever than training duration for carbon footprint.** Even
training for one-third the time (`{python} _short_days` days vs. `{python} _duration_days` days) in `{python} _g_poland.name` emits `{python} f"{_carbon_10p:.1f}"` tonnes of $\text{CO}_2$, which is **`{python} f"{_ratio_10p_30q:.1f}×"`** more than the full `{python} _duration_days`-day run in `{python} _g_quebec.name` (`{python} f"{_carbon_q:.1f}"` tonnes). Because grid carbon intensity differs by `{python} f"{_ci_ratio_pq:.0f}×"` and total facility emissions per day differ by `{python} f"{_ratio_pq:.0f}×"`, no plausible reduction in training time can compensate for a coal-heavy grid. For any organization serious
about sustainable AI, datacenter location is not a logistics detail but a
first-order systems design decision.
:::

---

## 5. Economic Angle: When Carbon Has a Price

Carbon pricing (through taxes or cap-and-trade) gives emissions a financial cost and
changes the economics of datacenter location. The cell below computes TCO with a carbon
price of `${python} _carbon_price`/tonne.

```{python}
from mlsysim.solvers import EconomicsModel

econ = EconomicsModel()
carbon_price = 50  # USD per tonne CO2

rows = []
for grid in grids:
    tco = econ.solve(fleet=fleet, duration_days=30, grid=grid)
    carbon_cost = (tco.carbon_footprint_kg / 1000) * carbon_price
    total = tco.tco_usd + carbon_cost
    rows.append([tco.region_name, f"${tco.tco_usd:,.0f}", f"${carbon_cost:,.0f}", f"${total:,.0f}"])

table(["Region", "TCO ($)", "Carbon Cost ($)", "Total ($)"], rows)
```

At `${python} _carbon_price`/tonne, carbon pricing adds `${python} f"{_ccost_q:,.0f}"` to the `{python} _duration_days`-day run in `{python} _g_quebec.name` (bringing total cost from `${python} f"{_tco_q.tco_usd:,.0f}"` to `${python} f"{_tot_q:,.0f}"`) versus `${python} f"{_ccost_p:,.0f}"` in `{python} _g_poland.name` (bringing total cost from `${python} f"{_tco_p.tco_usd:,.0f}"` to `${python} f"{_tot_p:,.0f}"`, a `${python} f"{_tot_p - _tot_q:,.0f}"` spread). At
higher carbon prices, this location differential grows proportionally.
